headline: National Zoological Park Organises Sunday Bird, Butterfly and Dragonfly Walks to Promote Science and Biodiversity Conservation among Citizens
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

National Zoological Park Organises Sunday Bird, Butterfly and Dragonfly Walks to Promote Science and Biodiversity Conservation among Citizens

06 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

The National Zoological Park (NZP), New Delhi, organised the third ‘Butterfly and Dragonfly Walk @ NZP’ and the 13th ‘Sunday Bird Walk @ NZP’, as part of its ongoing efforts to promote public participation in biodiversity monitoring, documentation of birds, butterflies and dragonflies, and awareness of wildlife conservation. The walks were conducted from 6:45 AM to 10:30 AM today under the expert guidance of Sh. Sanjay Tiwari and Sh. C.B. Maurya, butterfly and dragonfly expert, along with dedicated volunteers.

The programme received an enthusiastic response from bird and butterfly enthusiasts, nature lovers, students, wildlife photographers and citizens interested in biodiversity conservation. A total of 16 participants took part in the walks. The event was attended by the Director, National Zoological Park, zoo officials and resource experts, who guided and interacted with participants throughout the activity. During the walks, participants documented 44 bird species, with observations of more than 700 individual birds, along with 4 butterfly species, one dragonfly and one damselfly species each in the walk area. The relatively lower number of butterflies and dragonflies recorded was attributed to intermittent rainfall.

A notable highlight of the Bird Walk was the presence of more than 300 Painted Storks, which arrived at the National Zoological Park during the second week of August and have begun nesting on trees in and around the pond. Their arrival and nesting are encouraging indicators of the ecological value of the Zoo’s wetland and tree habitats. The nesting activity and breeding behaviour also provide an important opportunity for visitors, interns, volunteers and citizen scientists to observe and better understand natural bird behaviour and breeding ecology.

Sh. C.B. Maurya shared valuable insights into the ecology, behaviour and conservation of birds, butterflies and dragonflies, highlighting their vital ecological roles as pollinators, natural pest controllers and indicators of ecosystem health. The programme provided participants with an opportunity to connect with nature, enhance their species-identification skills and develop a deeper appreciation of biodiversity and its conservation.

Addressing the participants, Dr. Sanjeet Kumar, Director, National Zoological Park, highlighted that such nature walks provide valuable opportunities to strengthen field-identification skills, improve understanding of food webs, contribute to biodiversity documentation and foster a deeper appreciation of wildlife and biodiversity conservation. The programme concluded with an interactive discussion, a participant feedback session and a group photograph with the experts and zoo officials.

Participation in each Sunday Nature Walk is limited to 20–25 participants to ensure a meaningful and high-quality learning experience. Prior registration is mandatory and is accepted on a first-come, first-served basis. Interested participants may register through the designated Google Form, which remains open from Monday to Friday each week. The registration link is available on the official website of the National Zoological Park, New Delhi, and through the “NZP Sathi” mobile application.

The next nature walks—the 3rd ‘Sunday Insect and Spider Walk’ and the 14th ‘Sunday Bird Walk’—are scheduled to be held on Sunday, 20 September 2026.

headline: Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses a press conference on narcotics control in Panaji, the capital of Goa

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah addresses a press conference on narcotics control in Panaji, the capital of Goa

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, we will fulfil the resolve of a ‘Drug-free India’ by 2029

Just as Naxalism was eliminated from the country, we will similarly eliminate the problem of drugs

The roadmap for a ‘Drug-free India’ is based on four pillars – intelligence and operation-based enforcement, precursor and synthetic drugs control, demand and harm reduction, and capacity building and coordination

By adopting a quadrangular strategy, we are taking the necessary steps to curb the smuggling of drugs into the country through the routes of the Death Triangle and Death Crescent

Modi government has made the fight against drugs a national security priority

Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports, along with educational institutions, are resolving to make educational institutions drug-free

Through NCC, NSS and My Bharat, lakhs of ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat Mitras’ will be prepared

Modi Government has adopted a new approach to investigations through a Bottom-to-Top and Top-to-Bottom approach, with special emphasis on financial investigations and PIT-NDPS

From 2004 to 2014, 2.6 million kilograms of drugs worth ₹40,000 crore were seized, whereas from 2014 to 2026, more than 11.9 million kilograms of drugs worth ₹1.89 lakh crore were seized

Under the ‘Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan’, 250 million citizens have been reached and administered a pledge, while 570,000 citizens have been freed from drug addiction through treatment and rehabilitation

Department of Social Justice, Health Department, and Prison Administration are jointly working to triple the number of drug de-addiction centres to 1,751

A nationwide campaign is underway against fugitives who have fled the country after committing crimes; fugitives involved in economic offences, terrorism, narcotics and gang warfare have been brought back to face justice before Indian courts

06 SEP 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah today addressed a press conference on narcotics control in Panaji, the capital of Goa. On this occasion, Goa Chief Minister Shri Pramod Sawant was also present.

Addressing the press conference, Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that since Shri Narendra Modi became the Prime Minister, the Government of India has taken numerous steps to strengthen the country’s internal security. He said that when Modi Ji became the Prime Minister, the country was facing three formidable problems, which included rising terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, Naxalism, and the unrest created by several armed organisations in the Northeast. In addition, on the internal security front, the country was also greatly troubled by several bomb blasts. There were large-scale movements regarding the safety of women. It was precisely during that period that Modi Ji assumed the office of the Prime Minister of the country. Looking back from 2019 to now under his leadership, the situation has changed significantly. After the abrogation of Article 370 in Jammu and Kashmir, the feeling of separatism has reduced considerably. The figures of terrorism are gradually shrinking and moving towards zero, and Jammu and Kashmir has progressed on the path of development. Successful efforts have also been made to bridge the mental distance that existed between Jammu and Kashmir and the rest of the country. The five-decade-old problem of Naxalism has today almost become a thing of the past. Most of the people who imagined the Red Corridor have today surrendered by laying down arms and are joining the mainstream. Similarly, in the Northeast as well, around 11,000 youth have laid down arms. The Government of India has signed more than 14 agreements with them, and today the Northeast is also progressing on the path of development. After 2019, a campaign has also been launched against fugitives who fled after committing crimes. From 2019 to July 2026, 274 fugitives have been extradited from 36 countries. These include people involved in serious crimes such as economic offences, terrorism, narcotics, and gang wars. All of them have been brought before the courts of India. In the last three years, 401 Red Corner Notices have been issued. In 2026 alone, up to July, the entire process of issuing 182 Red Corner Notices has been successfully completed. For this, a new system has been created in the form of ‘BHARATPOL’. More than 14 central agencies and the police of all states are connected to ‘BHARATPOL’. A well-organised mechanism has been prepared through ‘BHARATPOL’ for the extradition of fugitives from every state. From 2019 to 2026, properties worth approximately ₹17,874 crore belonging to fugitives have been sealed or confiscated. The new criminal laws and justice codes have also made the path of legal action against fugitives easier.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that a systematic mechanism has also been prepared for cyber crimes, which is being monitored by Prime Minister Modi Ji himself. Today, the 1930 helpline has become an effective medium for protection against cyber crimes. Success has been achieved in implementing the three new criminal laws up to the police station level through the Ministry of Home Affairs with the cooperation of the states. He said that he thanks the Chief Minister of Goa and the Goa Police for implementing the new Nayaya Sanhita and the three criminal laws in such a short time and raising the conviction rate in the state to 53.2 per cent. This means that there has been an increase of approximately 30 per cent in the rate of securing convictions in registered FIRs.

Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah said that narcotics is a crime that can destroy our future generations. He said that the earnings from narcotics are also used for terrorism. The narco-terror module is active in many countries of the world, and the entire world is today grappling with this problem. He said that since 2019, we have put in place a robust system to curb it. For this, we have changed the systems, caught the networks, broken the financial chain, and also provided handholding to those addicted so as to free them from drugs. Shri Shah said that before 2014, this battle was fought in a piecemeal manner, and satisfaction was derived from making small seizures and catching small accused persons. But since 2019, the Modi government has made this subject a priority of national security. He said that the fight against drugs has moved beyond files and the actions of separate agencies and has now become a coordinated and continuous campaign at the national level.

Union Home Minister said that in 2019, a four-tier NCORD mechanism was created. A model for the formation of dedicated Anti-Narcotics Task Forces was sent to all states and Union Territories, and a Joint Coordination Committee was constituted. With the coordination of central agencies, state governments and their departments, a scientific method was adopted to address large networks, inter-state and international links, and operational gaps. The ‘1933’ Manas helpline was started for the rehabilitation of drug-addicted youth. The cadre of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) was restructured. A national database of narcotics offenders was created through the NIDAAN portal. Using CCTNS data and integrated data fusion, a data-based map of hotspots, modus operandi and seizures across the country was prepared. A new concept of investigation was adopted with both Bottom-to-Top and Top-to-Bottom approaches. He said that now even if a small packet of drugs is seized, it is examined where it originated from in the country. Similarly, if a large consignment is seized at the border, it is traced how it was going to reach the youth in the form of small packets. In this way, reverse investigation of the entire network has been started.

Shri Amit Shah said that special emphasis was given to financial investigation and PIT-NDPS, and a high-level dedicated task force was constituted. Technology-based investigation was started against the dark net, encrypted communication, crypto transactions and dead drop delivery. Work began on creating a dedicated Dark Net-Crypto Cell in the ANTF. An inter-ministerial mechanism was also created for precursors and synthetic drugs. He said that these efforts have yielded good results. Shri Shah said that from 2004 to 2014, under the rule of the opposition party, 26 lakh kilograms of drugs were seized, valued at approximately ₹40,000 crore. On the other hand, from 2014 to 2026 under the leadership of Modi Ji, this seizure has increased to more than 1 crore 19 lakh kilograms, valued at approximately ₹1 lakh 89 thousand crore. He said that from 2004 to 2014, 3 lakh 36 thousand kilograms of drugs were destroyed, whereas in 2014-26, 48 lakh 68 thousand kilograms of drugs have been destroyed.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that 10 apex meetings, 7 executive meetings, 277 state-level meetings and 16,798 district-level meetings of NCORD have been held. Agreements have been signed with 46 countries for international cooperation. Under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan, 25 crore citizens have been contacted and administered the oath. Under treatment and rehabilitation, 5 lakh 70 thousand citizens have been made drug-free. In Goa also, action has increased approximately three times during the same period.

Shri Amit Shah said that a three-year roadmap from July 2026 to July 2029 has been prepared. A decision has been taken to achieve all targets in a time-bound manner. He said that we are advancing the fight against drugs as one of the biggest national battles of the country. He said that the goal of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi is that by 2047, a drug-free youth power should form the foundation of a developed India. To make this mission successful, the Ministry of Home Affairs and all state governments are working together. He said that the period from 2026 to 2029 has been declared as mission mode. Timelines have been fixed, different ministries have been made accountable, measurable outcomes have been decided, and quarterly reviews along with outcome-based accountability will be ensured. He said that this roadmap is based on four pillars. First—intelligence and operation-based enforcement; second—precursor and synthetic drugs control; third—demand and harm reduction; and fourth—capacity building and coordination. He said that all these pillars together will prepare dossiers of drug kingpins, coordinate on backward-forward linkages, and tighten the noose through financial investigation of every case involving commercial quantities. He said that the BSF, CISF, Indian Coast Guard, Customs and DRI will carry out risk-based profiling and install scanners at land borders, ports, airports and cargo for sharper surveillance. The Home Minister said that the CBI, Ministry of External Affairs and Interpol will bring back the fugitives. The Enforcement Directorate, Financial Intelligence Unit and the banking system will catch the money trail.

Shri Amit Shah said that through the NCC, NSS and My Bharat, lakhs of ‘Nashamukti Mitra’ will be prepared. He said that the Ministry of Education, Youth Affairs and Sports, along with educational institutions, are taking a resolve to make educational institutions drug-free. The Social Justice, Health Department and Jail Administration together are going to increase the number of de-addiction centres threefold to 1,751. Approximately 10,000 volunteers will serve in this campaign. For capacity building, 7 per cent central assistance will be provided to create fully equipped Anti-Narcotics Task Forces in every state by March 2027. The Ministry of Home Affairs will make arrangements for forensic reports to be received within 30 days. In these four pillars, 25 components and more than 200 action points have been fixed in a time-bound manner.

Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah said that foreigners are welcome in India, but not with drugs. He said that by adopting the Quadrangular Approach, necessary action is being taken to curb the smuggling of drugs into the country through the routes of the Death Triangle and the Death Crescent. He said that just as Naxalism has been eliminated from the country, the problem of drugs will also be eliminated with the same resolve.

Assam’s medical colleges more than doubled from 7 in 2021 to 15; 9 more under construction: Vice President lauds CM Himanta Biswa Sarma

AIIMS Guwahati and three-tier cancer-care network strengthening Northeast’s healthcare ecosystem: Vice President

Vice President calls upon youth to stay away from substance abuse and contribute towards Nasha Mukt Bharat

06 SEP 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi

Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today urged graduating healthcare professionals to uphold compassion, ethics and scientific excellence, and dedicate their knowledge and skills to the service of humanity, while addressing the convocation ceremony of Srimanta Sankaradeva University of Health Sciences (SSUHS), Guwahati. He also presented the Dr. John Berry White Award for the years 2023, 2024 and 2025.

Addressing the convocation, he said that the University, named after Mahapurusha Srimanta Sankaradeva, has emerged as an important institution for health sciences education, research and public health. He appreciated its efforts to promote medical knowledge in local languages, including the publication of an Anglo-Assamese Dictionary of Medical Science and medical textbooks in Assamese.

The Vice President highlighted the transformation of India’s healthcare sector under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, referring to initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat. He noted that more than 44 crore Ayushman cards have been issued and recalled that the scheme has helped poor and middle-class families save an estimated Rs. 2 lakh crore in medical expenses.

Highlighting Assam’s healthcare progress, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the number of medical colleges in the State has more than doubled from seven in 2021 to 15, with another nine under construction. He also highlighted AIIMS Guwahati, the first AIIMS in the Northeast, and Assam’s three-tier cancer-care network, including the State’s first Proton Beam Therapy Centre.

The Vice President congratulated Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma and the Government of Assam for strengthening healthcare infrastructure and said that the changing healthcare landscape is enabling patients from outside Assam to increasingly seek advanced treatment in Guwahati.

Calling upon youth to lead healthy and disciplined lives, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan urged them to stay away from substance abuse and contribute towards building a Nasha Mukt Bharat. He also advised students to use social media constructively and not allow it to consume excessive time.

The Vice President said that young healthcare professionals have a crucial role in advancing the vision of a Viksit and Swasth Bharat, and wished the graduating students success in their future endeavours.

The convocation was attended by Governor of Assam Shri Lakshman Prasad Acharya; Chief Minister Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma; Minister of Medical Education & Research Shri Ashok Singhal; Education Minister Dr. Ranoj Pegu; Chief Secretary Dr. Ravi Kota; Vice-Chancellor of SSUHS Dr. Anup Kumar Barman, besides faculty members, researchers, students and parents.

headline: “Bring Industry Partners on Board from Day One”: Dr Jitendra Singh Calls for New Industry–R&D Partnership Model
fullText:
Ministry of Science & Technology

“Bring Industry Partners on Board from Day One”: Dr Jitendra Singh Calls for New Industry–R&D Partnership Model

Minister says early industry participation can make technologies market-ready and accelerate commercialisation

The Minister calls for industry-led common R&D platforms and continued government-industry engagement

06 SEP 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi

“The commercial arm should be in association with the lab right from day one.” With this message, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, called for a fundamental shift in the way industry and research institutions work together, during an interaction with CEOs, CSOs and COOs of industries at the 6th RISE Conclave at CSIR-IICB, Kolkata. He said that potential commercial partners should be identified and associated at the project-planning stage itself so that market requirements and practical considerations can shape the technology while it is still under development.

Responding to an industry suggestion that commercial partners should be brought in at the laboratory stage, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that early participation would allow industry to provide inputs on market dynamics, design, environmental sustainability, supply-chain requirements and commercial viability. He said, stressing that a technology should not reach the market only to discover that it needs modification to meet actual user requirements.

The interaction thereafter became a direct platform for industry to place specific technology and challenges before the Minister.

Critical minerals and indigenous technology also emerged as major areas of industry interest, with participants discussing rare-earth extraction, permanent magnets, recycling, lithium beneficiation and the recovery of strategic minerals such as vanadium and titanium. Industry representatives sought technological hand-holding from CSIR laboratories for scaling these technologies, while the discussion also covered exploration possibilities for rare earths and other critical minerals in eastern India.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need to leverage the capabilities being developed across CSIR institutions and other government scientific agencies.

The Minister also responded to industry inputs relating to space technology and specialised optical components. Dr. Jitendra Singh sought the relevant details and indicated that the space-related matter could be taken up with the Department of Space.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that regulatory simplification had already been undertaken and invited further specific inputs from industry, which could be taken up for consideration.

Dr. Jitendra Singh suggested exploring a common R&D facility for the foundry sector, with the industry coming together to articulate its requirements and the government facilitating the platform.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said there was no restriction on industries coming together to create such a platform and urged steel-sector players to collaborate. “We are ready to provide the forum. You come, all of you from all the different steel industries, as representatives, come as a group and say, ‘Provide us a forum.’ We’ll provide,” he said.

Bengal Chemicals and Pharmaceuticals raised the possibility of reviving indigenous production of anti-snake venom, pointing out that eastern India has distinct snake species and therefore specific regional requirements. Dr. Jitendra Singh advised the company to engage with the Health Ministry of W Bengal and stressed the importance of aligning any such effort with the scientific and public-health requirements.

A startup working in the venom and snakebite space subsequently presented technologies for identifying the species responsible for a snakebite and developing new antivenom solutions. Dr. Jitendra Singh welcomed the innovation but emphasised that such technologies would require proper scientific validation and clinical trials before wider adoption. He stressed that patient safety cannot be compromised and pointed the innovators towards the W Bengal Health Ministry for the necessary validation.

Throughout the interaction, Dr. Jitendra Singh repeatedly encouraged industry representatives to move from general discussions to specific, actionable requirements and assured that the government and scientific institutions would facilitate appropriate linkages. In his concluding remarks, he said, “You tell us what we can do for you or what we are not doing for you, or what we can do better for you,” underlining the government’s readiness to respond to clearly articulated industry needs.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also made it clear that such engagement should not remain restricted to formal events. “If there are further inputs, you are always free. Not that you have to wait for a formal occasion like this,” he said, inviting industry to continue engaging with the concerned institutions. The interaction at the 6th RISE Conclave thus reinforced a clear model for strengthening India’s technology ecosystem, industry as a partner from the beginning of R&D, scientific institutions as technology enablers, and government as a facilitator for taking promising technologies from the laboratory to the market and ultimately to wider societal application.
